text:
Zack: kicking off a burst-bank scaling experiment — objective: measure scale-up time and tail-latency when burst credits are consumed across mixed-priority workloads. plan: replay harness v2 + synthetic micro-bursts + steady ramp. toggles: kernel_selector=heuristic-v3, kv_cache=enabled, batching=auto. running on dedicated pool d-6. anyone object?
Maya: lgtm. can we include an apples-to-apples run with kernel_selector=int8_fallback too?
Jon: also capture hot vs cold KV hit rates. include a run with kv_priming=off for comparison.
Lee: added run matrix to bench script. snippet: `./bench --replay --seed=42 --microburst=200rps --burst-bank=100 --kernels=heuristic-v3,int8 --kv=on,priming-off`
ops-bot: bench-harness v2 deployed to staging at 2041234572 :robot_face: 
Carla: quick note — cap batch_size to 32 to avoid batching explosion on microbursts.
Zack: running first run now (heuristic-v3, kv-priming=on). attaching quick results: p50=18ms, p95=86ms, p99=240ms, kv-hit=72%, scale-up=12s.
Maya: p99 looks high. do we see kernel switch spikes?
Zack: yes — trace shows kernel flip at ~2.7s after surge start. log excerpt: `[INFO] kernel-selector: heuristic-v3 -> cuda_int8 at t=2.7s; first post-switch batch latency +120ms`
Jon: suggests prefill helps. try pre-populating KV by replaying ~20% of sessions 30s before surge.
Lee: queued a matched run with kv_prefill. results: p95=54ms, p99=130ms, kv-hit=94%, scale-up ~11s.
Carla: scale-up still dominated by node spin-up time rather than kernel warmup. maybe reduce burst-bank credits to avoid node launch churn.
Zack: scheduling next matrix: burst-bank=40 credits, batch_cap=16. run in ~15m.
ops-bot: run started 2041234590 (bench id bench-2041234567)
Maya: reminder to collect kernel IO wait / GPU memcpy counters, attach trace id bench-2041234567.
Zack: grabbing traces now. early takeaway: apples-to-apples priming vs no-priming => ~35% improvement at p99 with kv-prefill. proposal: enable lightweight prespin (keep 1 spare node for bursts) + enable kv-prefill for heavy-priority routes.
Jon: +1. also file a perf-regression ticket for kernel-switch penalty — consider async kernel swap to hide the cost.
Zack: will open ticket and follow up in eng-runtime sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
